result: Touch domes emerge at E16.5 as patches of K17-positive keratinocytes and K8-positive Merkel cells adjacent to primary hair follicles. Between E15.5 and E16.5, Merkel cells shift from predominantly hair follicle localization to touch dome localization, with a dramatic increase in Merkel cell numbers per touch dome (order of magnitude increase) that is independent of follicle growth.
evaluation: Reviewer #1 explicitly affirms this finding, stating the study 'defines the time windows within which touch dome precursors appear and produce Merkel cells.' Reviewer #2 acknowledges 'touch dome patches emerge at E16.5' without questioning the data. No reviewer challenges the temporal dynamics or quantification of Merkel cell distribution.

result: BMP4-expressing dermal cells (CFP-high cells in Bmp4CFP reporter mice) cluster near developing touch domes. At E15.5, these cells are prominent in dermal condensates of hair follicles, and by E16.5-E18.5, they cluster at hair follicle-epidermal junctures in proximity to Merkel cell clusters. CFP immunoreactivity appears in touch-dome keratinocytes at adult but not embryonic stages.
evaluation: Reviewer #2 explicitly states 'The identity of the BMP4-expressing dermal fibroblasts has not been determined although it has been mentioned in the abstract' and questions whether these are truly the BMP4-expressing cells affected by noggin overexpression. The reviewer requests confirmation of cell identity and better specificity of manipulation, indicating the evidence is incomplete.

result: Epidermal Noggin overexpression at E14.5 disrupts touch dome formation (reducing K17-positive keratinocytes, Merkel cells, and innervation) but not hair follicle specification, demonstrating a temporally distinct requirement for BMP signaling. When Noggin is induced at E17.5, touch dome components are unaffected, identifying E14.5-E17.5 as a critical window for BMP signaling in touch dome development.
evaluation: Reviewer #1 acknowledges the study 'identifies an apparently discrete population of BMP expressing mesenchymal cells that contribute to touch dome development.' Reviewer #2 describes the noggin overexpression results without challenging the conclusions. While Reviewer #2 questions the specificity of the manipulation, they do not dispute the temporal findings or the differential effects on touch domes versus hair follicles.

result: Touch dome innervation begins at E16.5 when NFH-positive branches first contact Merkel cells. By E18.5, there is exuberant neuronal sprouting with robust innervation extending superficially and laterally to Merkel cell clusters. By P21, NFH-positive branches terminate on the inferior aspect of Merkel cells in the mature pattern.
evaluation: Reviewer #3 states 'It was unclear to me from the images that the touch dome was hyper-innervated at E18.5 followed by a retraction during postnatal development' and requests quantification at these ages to clarify the finding. This indicates the reviewer found the evidence for exuberant sprouting at E18.5 insufficient without additional quantitative support.

result: Two distinct neuronal populations innervate touch domes during development: tdTomato-positive (TrkC lineage) afferents that terminate on Merkel cells and tdTomato-negative (NFH-positive, TrkC-negative) afferents that extend more superficially into spinous and granular layers. The tdTomato-negative population is transient, with only TrkC lineage innervation persisting in mature touch domes by P21.
evaluation: Reviewer #1 explicitly affirms the study 'identifies a previously unrecognized population of TrkC negative NFH positive sensory terminals that transiently innervate the touch dome with a pattern distinct from that of those neurons associated more intimately with Merkel cells.' No reviewer challenges this novel finding or the characterization of the two populations.

result: K17-expressing keratinocytes are necessary to establish touch dome innervation during development. Ablation of K17-lineage cells dramatically reduced K17 area, Merkel cell numbers, and NFH-positive terminal endings (median decreased from 16 to 2), demonstrating that touch-dome epidermal cells are required to establish innervation patterns and terminal architecture of NFH-positive afferents.
evaluation: Reviewer #1 states the study 'establishes the necessity and sufficiency of K17 expressing epithelial cells for touch dome innervation.' Reviewer #2 acknowledges the ablation results without challenge. The necessity claim is well-supported by reviewer acceptance.

result: Overexpression of Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) in K17-expressing keratinocytes from E16.5-E18.5 expands the K17-positive population and increases NFH-positive skin innervation without affecting Merkel cell numbers, suggesting K17-expressing keratinocytes are sufficient to recruit NFH-positive innervation.
evaluation: Reviewer #2 raises a critical concern: 'Although ablation of K17-expressing keratinocytes reduced the number of Merkel cells, overexpressing shh in K17-expressing keratinocytes expanded the K17 population and increased NFH-positive skin innervation but did not affect the number of Merkel cells...it is not understood why the number of Merkel cells was not also increased.' Reviewer #3 notes this experiment 'is relegated to a single supplementary image' and 'was not quantified,' requesting quantification and promotion to main figures. These concerns indicate uncertainty about the interpretation and completeness of evidence.

result: Merkel cells are not required for proper touch dome innervation during embryonic development. In Atoh1 null mice lacking Merkel cells, the structure of touch-dome afferents (terminal branches, branch order, complexity) at E18.5 did not differ from controls, though Merkel cells may be involved in refining sensory arbors postnatally.
evaluation: Reviewer #1 explicitly states the study 'builds upon previous studies that demonstrate the dispensibility of Merkel cells for the recruitment of sensory terminals to the vicinity of touch domes.' No reviewer challenges the Atoh1 knockout data or the conclusion that Merkel cells are dispensable for embryonic innervation establishment.

result: The authors propose that touch domes co-opt evolutionarily conserved placodal mechanisms to assemble mechanosensory complexes, with K17-lineage keratinocytes driving selective targeting of two distinct populations of myelinated afferents. K17-lineage cell types are proposed to be necessary and sufficient for both development and maintenance of NFH-positive afferents.
evaluation: Reviewer #1 describes the work as 'thoughtfully discussed' and representing 'a significant contribution.' Reviewer #3 requests 'a summary illustration or graphical abstract describing the process of touch dome development' to better tie together the findings, suggesting the model is acceptable but presentation could be improved. No reviewer challenges the conceptual framework or conclusions.
